questions.q: What is the actual code fix for this bug?
options: Restore the MERGE's ON clause to match on transaction_id instead of store_id and sale_date
Add a WHERE clause to silver.sales_clean to filter out duplicate stores
Increase the reconciliation tolerance from $0.01 to $1.00
Delete gold.category_breakdown and only keep gold.daily_sales_summary
questions.explain: The fix restores the exact match condition Lesson 5 already proved correct — one column swapped back on the ON clause.

questions.q: Why isn't fixing the ON clause alone enough to resolve the ticket?
options: Delta Lake requires dropping and recreating the entire table after any ON clause change
The ON clause fix only applies to gold.category_breakdown, not silver.sales_clean
Every MERGE between March 1st and the fix date already ran with the wrong key, so silver.sales_clean still carries corrupted data for that range until it's backfilled
Fixing the ON clause automatically repairs all historical data with no further action
questions.explain: The fix only protects future runs — the affected date range has to be reprocessed with the corrected MERGE to repair the existing corruption.

questions.q: After backfilling silver.sales_clean, what else must be rebuilt?
options: The original bronze.sales_raw table needs to be deleted and re-ingested
Both Gold tables, since they were already built from the corrupted Silver data for that range
Only gold.daily_sales_summary; gold.category_breakdown is unaffected
Nothing else — Gold tables update themselves automatically whenever Silver changes
questions.explain: Both Gold tables inherited the corruption from the bad Silver merge, so both need to be regenerated from the corrected Silver data for the affected range.

questions.q: How is the fix actually proven to have worked?
options: Reading through the corrected MERGE statement once more and confirming it looks right
Re-running Lesson 9's exact reconciliation query across the affected date range and confirming every row returns diff = 0.00
Asking the Regional Manager if the dashboard looks better now
Checking that the job finished without throwing an error
questions.explain: Re-running the same diagnostic tool that caught the bug, and getting a clean result, is what separates 'I think it's fixed' from 'I proved it's fixed.'

questions.q: What makes transaction_id a durable match key when store_id + sale_date isn't?
options: store_id and sale_date are not real columns in this schema
transaction_id is uniqueness-guaranteed by the source system; no combination of business columns like store_id and sale_date carries that same guarantee
transaction_id is simply a longer string, which always sorts more reliably
transaction_id is guaranteed unique only because it was chosen first in Lesson 5
questions.explain: A match key is only as safe as the uniqueness the source system actually promises — transaction_id is the one column here that promise applies to.
